s: With reference to the historicity of the Jain Tirthankaras, which one of the following statements is correct?

o: The world runs according to an eternal law of decay and development and has no creator god.
The world is governed by the Vedic sacrificial order.
The world is periodically created by the Tirthankaras.
The world was created and is continuously controlled by a personal creator god.
x: Jainism is non-theistic and holds that the world functions according to an eternal law of decay and development rather than the will of a creator god.

Accumulating material possessions and fulfilling worldly desires
Stopping the inflow of karma and shedding accumulated karma through penance
Following fate without undertaking spiritual discipline
x: Jain liberation involves stopping the inflow of karma and shedding accumulated karma, or nirjara, through penance, ultimately leading to Kevala Jnana and the Siddha state.
tq: Use the cause-and-effect chain from karmic bondage to liberation.

With reference to the monastic practices and texts of Jainism and Buddhism, consider the following statements:
1. Digambara Jain monks traditionally remain unclothed.
2. Buddhist monks wear saffron robes.
3. Jain canonical texts are known as the Agamas and are associated with Ardhamagadhi.
4. The Buddhist canonical collection is the Tripitaka, written in Pali.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements correctly describe the monastic traditions and textual languages or collections associated with Jainism and Buddhism.
tq: Verify each religion-text and religion-monastic pair instead of relying on one familiar association.
sec: Jainism and Buddhism compared  [other exams]

s: Which of the following correctly expresses a doctrinal difference between Jainism and Buddhism?
o: Jainism spread widely abroad, whereas Buddhism remained confined to India.
Jainism associates liberation with kevala jnana, while Buddhism associates it with nirvana or Buddhahood.
Buddhism accepts an eternal soul in all things, while Jainism teaches anatta.
Jainism alone accepts karma and rebirth, while Buddhism rejects both.
x: Jainism uses the concept of kevala jnana, while Buddhism refers to nirvana or Buddhahood. Buddhism, unlike Jainism, spread extensively outside India.
tq: Identify the reversed doctrinal and geographical comparisons before choosing the precise distinction.
sec: Jainism and Buddhism compared  [other exams]

s: The four vows of Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya and Aparigraha are traditionally associated with which teacher?
x: Parshvanatha taught the four vows, collectively associated with chaturyama. Mahavira later added Brahmacharya as the fifth vow.
tq: Use the teacher-versus-teaching trap to distinguish Parshvanatha's four vows from Mahavira's addition.
sec: Panchamahavratas - five vows and the fifth added by Mahavira

s: Which one of the following was added by Mahavira as the fifth vow to the earlier four vows of Jainism?
x: Brahmacharya, or celibacy, was added by Mahavira as the fifth vow. Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya and Aparigraha were the four vows associated with Parshvanatha.
tq: Discriminate the later addition from the four pre-existing vows.
sec: Panchamahavratas - five vows and the fifth added by Mahavira

s:
With regard to Jain ethical practice among householders, consider the following statements:
1. Householders observe milder forms of the vows known as Anuvratas.
2. Non-adultery is included among the householders' milder vows.
3. Householders are expected to give food to the needy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Jain householders observe Anuvratas, which include non-injury, non-stealing, non-adultery, truth and non-possession. Providing food to the needy is also part of the stated household ethic.
tq: Check the complete list of householders' obligations rather than confusing them with the Mahavratas of ascetics.
sec: Panchamahavratas - five vows and the fifth added by Mahavira

s: Vaddamanu, also known as Vardhamanapuram, is associated with which of the following?
o: A Jain centre in Guntur associated with Samprati's basadi or vihara
A Buddhist centre in Guntur founded by Gautama Buddha
A cave complex in Anantapur associated only with the Ajivikas
A Jain centre in YSR Kadapa built by Indra III
x: Vaddamanu or Vardhamanapuram is located in Guntur and is associated with a basadi or vihara built by Samprati in Mahavira's name.
tq: Use the place-person association and reject the nearby Andhra Jain centres with different patrons.

s: Samprati, described as the ‘Ashoka of Jainism’, is associated with which activity in Andhra?
o: Beginning the Hanamkonda inscription with a Jain prayer
Building the Jain kshetra at Danavulapadu
Building a Jain basadi or vihara at Vaddamanu in Mahavira's name
x: Samprati, Ashoka's grandson, is associated with constructing a Jain basadi or vihara at Vaddamanu in Mahavira's name.
tq: Match the patron with his specific construction activity rather than with another Andhra Jain association.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Indra III — Jain basadi at Vaddamanu
Mahapadma Nanda — Jain kshetra at Danavulapadu
x: Kharavela is associated with building a Jain vihara near Vaddamanu. Danavulapadu is associated with Rashtrakuta Indra III, while the other associations are incorrect.
tq: Apply the wrong-builder trap by linking each ruler to the centre actually associated with him.

s: Mahapadma Nanda is said to have contributed to the history of Jainism in Andhra by
o: building a Jain kshetra at Danavulapadu
constructing caves in the Nallamala hills
x: Mahapadma Nanda is said to have conquered Andhra and propagated Jainism there. The other activities are associated with different persons or developments.
tq: Identify the ruler's deed and avoid the swapped-patron trap.

s: Danavulapadu, an important Jain centre in Andhra Pradesh, is located in
o: Hanamkonda and was built by Prolaraju
Guntur district and was built by Samprati
Kurnool district and was built by Mahapadma Nanda
Jammalamadugu in YSR Kadapa district and was built by Rashtrakuta Indra III
x: Danavulapadu is a Jain kshetra at Jammalamadugu in YSR Kadapa district, associated with Rashtrakuta ruler Indra III.
tq: Combine location and patronage to defeat the close-place and swapped-builder distractors.

s: Rayalaseema is described as a Jain corridor primarily because
o: the capital of the Rashtrakutas was located there
the Buddhist route from Sarnath to Bodh Gaya passed through the region
the Bhadrabahu–Chandragupta route to Shravanabelagola passed through Kurnool and Anantapur
all Jain Tirthankaras were born in Rayalaseema
x: The Bhadrabahu–Chandragupta route to Shravanabelagola passed through Kurnool and Anantapur, supporting the description of Rayalaseema as a Jain corridor.
tq: Follow the route-based clue and distinguish it from unsupported origin and capital claims.

s: The ascetic caves associated with the Jain presence in the Rayalaseema region are found in the
x: The Jain ascetic caves of the Rayalaseema corridor are associated with the Erramala and Nallamala hills.
tq: Use the location-specific pair rather than selecting a broader but unsupported hill system.

s:
Consider the following statements about the early Kakatiyas:
1. They were Jains in their early phase.
2. Their overlords included the Rashtrakutas and Kalyani Chalukyas, who were Jains.
3. Siddeshwara Charitra confirms their Jain association.
4. Prolaraju's Hanamkonda inscription begins with a Jain prayer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements describe the Jain association of the early Kakatiyas, their overlords, the literary evidence and Prolaraju's Hanamkonda inscription.

s: Which of the following sets contains only rulers who were contemporaries of Mahavira?
o: Chandragupta Maurya, Chetaka, Samudragupta and Ajatashatru
x: The rulers listed as contemporaries of Mahavira are Bimbisara and Ajatashatru of Magadha, Chetaka of the Lichchhavis and Pradyota of Avanti.
tq: Separate the contemporary ruler group from rulers belonging to later imperial periods.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the teachers contemporary with Mahavira?
o: Pakudha Kachchayana — teacher contemporary with Mahavira
Purana Kassapa — teacher contemporary with Mahavira
x: Parshvanatha preceded Mahavira and was not a contemporary teacher of his period. Purana Kassapa, Pakudha Kachchayana and Makkhali Gosala are included among the contemporary teachers.
tq: Find the one anachronistic figure by separating Mahavira's predecessor from his contemporaries.

s: Anekantavada is significant in modern ethical and social thought because it is regarded as a basis for
o: exclusive adherence to one philosophical doctrine
tolerance, pluralism and acceptance of multiple viewpoints
rejection of all forms of non-violence
x: Anekantavada recognises the many-sided nature of reality and is therefore cited as a basis of pluralism and tolerance.
tq: Apply the philosophical principle to a social situation rather than treating it as a mere technical term.

s: Which of the following factors contributed to the limited mass appeal and later decline of Jainism?
o: Severe austerities, loss of royal patronage and the Digambara–Svetambara split
Complete absence of monastic institutions and rejection of ahimsa
Exclusive dependence on overseas expansion and maritime trade
Acceptance of Vedic sacrifice and Brahmana supremacy
x: Jainism's severe austerities limited its mass appeal, while loss of royal patronage and the Digambara–Svetambara split contributed to its later decline.
tq: Select the option that combines the stated social, political and sectarian causes without reversing Jain doctrine.

o: the Buddhist monastic code in Pali
a Jain practice associated with voluntary fasting unto death
the first sermon of Mahavira at Sarnath
the coronation ritual of Jain kings
x: Sallekhana is a Jain practice involving voluntary fasting unto death under prescribed spiritual conditions.
